The package (units: aircraft, teams, or people for the Bomba lines):
- cl415: CL-415MP scooper (APMM); up to 1, 10 days; works in kalimantan, elsewhere only after a request (earliest day 4); fact.
- helicopters: Medium helicopters with buckets (NADMA, APMM, TUDM); up to 3, 14 days; works in kalimantan, elsewhere only after a request (earliest day 4); fact.
- ground_teams: Lance teams of 6 from the 52 personnel; up to 2, 13 days; works in kalimantan, elsewhere only after a request (earliest day 5); assumption.
- bomba_domestic: Bomba firefighters on Malaysian fires; up to 100 people, 14 days; works in malaysia; assumption.
- ground_task_force: Bomba ground task force with pumps; up to 150 people, 14 days; works in kalimantan, elsewhere only after a request (earliest day 7); assumption.
Domestic Bomba works only on Malaysian soil. Everything else is deployed to Indonesia, accepted for Kalimantan only.
What the research says (cite as R1 to R10):
R1 Rank by influence on the target, never by fire power or distance.
R2 Fire power measures flame; smouldering peat makes 3 to 6 times more particulate per kg burned for less heat. Never rank peat fires by fire power.
R3 Send only what can finish the job or hold the advancing edge; half-suppressed peat relights.
R4 Attack a cluster from its edge and as a whole, never its middle; unsuppressed fire within about 10 km relights it.
R5 Aircraft knock down surface flame near water; they do not extinguish peat. The whole air package would saturate only 4 to 6 ha of deep peat.
R6 Ground lance teams are the only tool that ends peat fires: 0.25 to 3 ha a team-day (central 1). About 1 ha of active front per detection (0.3 to 3).
R7 Domestic fires are fast, need no consent, and 200 to 300 km away a small one can matter as much as a large one abroad.
R8 Value suppression only until the rains; rain ended the haze in 1997, 2015 and 2019.
R9 Influence holds only for its wind; prefer plans that hold up across the wind members.
R10 A plan needing new Indonesian consent is a request with a lag, not an assignment.

payload.detail:
Reduce the fire-smoke PM2.5 reaching Kuala Lumpur and surroundings over the 14 days from 12 October by suppressing, as whole clusters and from day 1 where possible, the specific complexes that carry the largest shares of KL's coming smoke. The measure is ug/m3 removed from the target's mean and hours of API above 100 avoided, judged against the ceiling in each wind member, not tools used or fires counted.

One question is before the Committee: which fire complexes Malaysia puts out first, with what, from when, to clear the haze over Kuala Lumpur and surroundings, and what the air there will be afterwards. With no plan the target's mean is 54.53 ug/m3 (W1), 43.28 (W2), 56.57 (W3) and 75.24 (W4), with 255 hours above API 100 in W4; the ceiling — all that extinguishing every fire from day 1 could remove — is 14.64, 4.95, 18.06 and 34.57 ug/m3 respectively, so most of that air is beyond our reach and the argument is over the part that is not. Objective, weights and premises are frozen and will not move: klBenefit 0.40, robustness 0.25, feasibility 0.15, diplomacy 0.10, cost 0.05, side benefits 0.05. Seats draft blind from their own premise; constraints on where the package may work are the validator's, not this chair's, and I will decide by the rule and speak last.

Weights, frozen: klBenefit 0.40, robustness 0.25, feasibility 0.15, diplomacy 0.10, cost 0.05, sideBenefits 0.05. One substantive move: robustness 0.20 to 0.25, with klBenefit taking the 0.05 to keep the set at one. Reason: the ceiling runs from 4.95 ug/m3 (W2) to 34.57 ug/m3 (W4), a seven-fold spread, and the influence ranking inverts across members — the Jambi complexes (C005 13.21%, C014 11.06% in W1) fall to 2.53% and 2.26% in W2, while C007 rises from 2.86% to 8.91% and C121 from 3.02% to 8.06%. Per R9, influence holds only for its wind, so a plan that wins in one member and fails in another is worth less than the point estimate suggests. All other weights stand at default.

Premises: Air Quality: Best achievable for KL's air if Indonesia grants every request made, including outside Kalimantan; state the lag each request costs (R10).; Meteorology: Maximise the worst outcome across W1 to W4 — judge the plan by its weakest wind member, not its best.; Peat Science: Commit only to fronts that can actually be finished at 0.25 to 3 ha per team-day (R6); no half-suppressed peat (R3).; Force Command: Strictly inside what Indonesia accepted on 18 September: Kalimantan only, nothing new asked, day 1 starts available.; Air Operations: Most ug/m3 removed per aircraft-day and per person-day; treat the air package's 4 to 6 ha of deep peat (R5) as the hard limit on what air buys.; Domestic Fire: Only what Malaysia controls today: domestic Bomba on Malaysian complexes, no consent, from day 1 (R7).; Health: Fewest person-hours above API 100 soonest across the 9 DOE stations, weighted to the W4 peak of 189.94 ug/m3 and its 20 h above API 200.; Sarawak: Protect KL and Sarawak jointly: prefer complexes whose suppression serves both populations..

payload.headline: Mass every Kalimantan-eligible asset on C007 near Manismata, the complex most dangerous to both KL (8.91% of W2's ceiling) and Sarawak, instead of splitting them thin.
requests: No new Indonesian consent required — all four assets already work in Kalimantan under the current arrangement; this plan asks Jakarta only to keep that access open for the full 14-day horizon on C007 specifically.
payload.rationale: Ranked by influence, not size or distance (R1): among Kalimantan complexes, C007 (Manismata, West Kalimantan) carries the highest share of KL's coming smoke in W2 (8.91%, the weak-wind inter-monsoon member) and is competitive across the rest (W1 2.86%, W3 3.26%, W4 1.33%). West Kalimantan directly borders Sarawak, and my mandate is to protect Sarawak and KL jointly; Serian's API 521 emergency this week is fed by this same Kalimantan corridor. C007 is peat-dominant (peat 0.46, night 0.70), so per R2/R5 aircraft alone cannot finish it — only ground crews end peat (R6). I therefore commit the full ground package (150 ground_task_force + 2 ground_teams) to one cluster rather than splitting across C003 and C007 as I first tested: that split plan (simulated) returned only 0.26% of the ceiling centrally and 0.03% worst-member, because neither complex was fully suppressed and peat relit (R3/R4). Concentrating all ground force plus all air assets (1 CL-415, 3 helicopters; open sea 13 km away per C007's record) on C007 alone gives the best chance of finishing one cluster rather than touching two and finishing neither. All assets stay inside existing Kalimantan authorization, so no consent lag applies (R10).

payload.rationale: C003 (Seruyan, Central Kalimantan) is the top Kalimantan complex by influence (R1): share of KL's coming smoke 3.05% (W1), 7.82% (W2), 5.16% (W3), 1.34% (W4); absolute 0.45/0.39/0.93/0.46 ug/m3 (get_influence). A tested split with C007 (next-highest, W2 8.91%) gave an identical central/worst-member result (0.24%/0.04%) with only a marginally better optimistic tail (1.52% vs 1.35%), while diluting ground force per complex — against the mandate to concentrate, not scatter. C007's cl415/helicopters are unchanged - no seat offered evidence against R5's logic there, and it needs no consent. Domestic Fire's evidence - C121/C120 are surface fires (peat 0.00), burned only 1 and 3 of 30 days - moved me to cut bomba_domestic from 14 to 4 days, releasing the surge to reserve. payload.gist: Deciding by the frozen rule: P22 has the best weighted score (0.831); I explain it and state plainly where it falls short of the code plan P11 and of the ceiling.

payload.detail:
Act now: Move what needs no consent today: CL-415 to C007 days 1-10, three helicopters days 1-14, 60 Bomba to C121 and 40 to C120 days 1-4. Remaining Bomba held in reserve, not dispersed for appearance.

Ask: One combined request: two lance teams from day 5 and the 150-person task force from day 7, together at C020 (Simpang, Jambi). Granted, it carries most of the 11.11% of ceiling; refused, we sit near 6.86%.

Share: Command and safety of every ground crew at C020 remain with Indonesian authorities; Malaysia supplies personnel and equipment under their direction. Wind-member attribution and detection data for C020 passed with the request through the NADMA-BNPB channel.

The rule was frozen before any plan existed: best weighted score. P22 scores 0.831 against P19's 0.688 and P1's 0.613, carried by klBenefit 1.00 and robustness 0.93 - one Sumatra ask rather than two, so R10's lag is incurred once. Engine: expected 11.11% of the ceiling, worst wind 5.60%, pessimistic 5.47%, optimistic 12.61%. It beats the consent-free code plan P10 (6.45%, worst wind 1.11%). It does not beat P11, the code plan that assumes consent: 15.49% expected, 9.24% worst wind, spread over three Sumatra complexes. Two honest statements follow. The gain is modest - about a ninth of what putting out every fire from day 1 could remove; against W4's 34.57 ug/m3 ceiling the worst-wind case is under 2 ug/m3 (my arithmetic). And P22's own record states its figures were not re-simulated.

Minority report: Red Cell and Health hold, unresolved, that the plan protects the mild member W2 while leaving W4 - the worst exposure, ceiling 34.57 ug/m3 - thin; C020's W4 share is 6.40% against C005's 11.71%. The Chair records a second objection in the plan's own text: P22's figures were not re-run through simulate_plan and are carried from P7 (expected 6.86%, worst wind 1.73%). The rule chose on numbers the engine has not yet confirmed for these lines. Nothing was argued against P22 in cross-examination, which is absence of challenge, not confirmation.
